[LERR.1.4.1] **When.** A computation has **no honest answer** —
no value, `null` included, would be true of it. That is
the whole test ([LERR.1.4.9]).

Where the input came from does not enter into it. An `Int` division
by zero is a trap whether the denominator is a literal or a
sensor reading, because in neither case is there an answer. A `Float`
operation always has one, an infinity or a NaN included ([LDET.3.6.2]),
so no `Float` arithmetic traps.

idris.name: Lerr_1_4_1__result
idris.note: An evaluation yields a value or a trap: no honest answer, null included. The trap is a constructor, so no value can stand in for it.
